cohort: Neonates between 0 and 28 days of life born at full term (37-40 weeks of gestation), exclusively breastfed, and having an axillary temperature of >37.5°C/100.4°F and clinical signs of dehydration.
finding: The incidence of dehydration fever was 4.71/100 neonates (152 out of 3225 neonatal admissions), with the most common predisposing factors being primiparity, poor breastfeeding establishment, and cesarean section delivery.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was found to be a predisposing factor for dehydration fever in exclusively breastfed neonates.
